1. Model consistently overestimates prices in early forecast periods, especially after sharp upward spikes — reduce initial forecast values by 2–5% relative to recent history.

2. Model exhibits strong upward bias in the first 5–10 days of forecast horizon — apply a downward correction of 1–3% for the first 5–10 forecast days.

3. After a price spike, model tends to overshoot and continue rising — cap forecast growth rate at 1.5x recent average daily change.

4. Model underestimates prices in late forecast horizon (last 5–10 days) — apply a 1–3% upward adjustment for final 5–10 days, especially if true outcome shows mean reversion.

5. Model fails to capture mean reversion in 30-day forecasts — if true outcome shows a clear downward trend after a peak, reduce forecast slope by 20–40% for the remainder of the horizon.

6. Model overfits recent volatility — if history shows high variance, reduce forecast smoothness by applying a 10–15% dampening factor to avoid overreacting to short-term noise.

7. Model ignores long-term trend — if true outcome shows a clear downward trend over 30 days, adjust forecast to align with 10–15 day moving average of history, not just recent peak.
